Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935) unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held for this code. research_rationale: The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6403 (signed November 4, 1933; the page heading names the application of Kaplan Brothers) records that a Code of Fair Competition for the Artificial Flower and Feather Industry "has been heretofore approved by me", that hearings were granted to the applicants, and that no case of injustice and extreme hardship was made out. The only command is "do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be and it is hereby denied". Under the reviewed shared analysis, an order that denies an application for exemption from a code commands nothing after it issues: its command is exhausted by performance on the date it is signed, and the applicant's continuing obligation is the code's own operation, which the approving order governs and which ended with the repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"). The repeal is therefore a later event of this order, not its end.
savings_reason: The denial was performed on the date it was signed, so nothing remains to be saved from it; the applicants' obligations after the denial arose from the code, which the approving order governed and which was repealed on June 14, 1935 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113). Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before the repeal are accrued, and the section 5 exemption for completed action is an accrued effect (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5).

research_rationale: The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6430 (signed November 14, 1933) is a one-command order: after reciting the application, hearings and findings under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, the President wrote "do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved" for the Code of Fair Competition for the All-Metal Insect Screen Industry. Under the reviewed shared analysis, the first end of such a command is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. savings_reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued, and the section 5 exemption for action completed while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5). Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after the repeal.

No held record shows this code cancelled, modified or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.
scope_check: The command approves the whole Code of Fair Competition for the All-Metal Insect Screen Industry under section 3(a) of Title I. independent_command_check: The order contains no appointment, delegation, direction to an agency or other command independent of the code approval.
